title: Energetic Protection, Monotonicity and Switching Far from Equilibrium
abstract: At equilibrium, the ratio of two steady-state probabilities is a Boltzmann factor, set by a free-energy difference. Such ratios are the natural, normalization-independent readouts of both thermodynamics and information processing, and are often used as a measure of fidelity in biophysical systems. What becomes of these ratios once a system is driven from equilibrium, where the Boltzmann factor no longer holds? Representing Markov processes as graphs and their steady states as averages over a distribution on spanning trees, the \emph{arboreal distribution}, we track the ratio $π_i/π_j$ under driving along \emph{energetic edges}, where detailed balance is broken, relative to its equilibrium value. Our central finding is that a chosen ratio can stay exactly locked to its equilibrium value arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a phenomenon we call \emph{energetic protection}, whenever an algebraic equality between spanning-tree weights holds. Just as detailed balance constrains rates around cycles, energetic protection constrains weights across trees, providing a new mechanism for robustness against fluctuations in the driving force, such as variations in ATP concentration. Away from this equality, single-edge driving collapses the response onto two arboreal coefficients and forces it to be monotonic, so nonmonotonic single-edge control is impossible at any strength. With two energetic edges, protection and monotonicity combine into a \emph{thermodynamic switch} that holds a function at its equilibrium value for as long as desired and releases it sharply. Equilibrium is known for the limits it places on information processing. We show that new constraints, both no-go principles and exact invariances, survive far from equilibrium. These results reveal how the localization of energy expenditure governs the functional logic of nonequilibrium systems in physics and biology.
summary: This paper develops a graph-theoretic framework to study how information processing capabilities are constrained when physical systems operate far from equilibrium. The central finding is 'energetic protection,' which reveals that specific ratios can remain invariant despite strong external driving forces if certain algebraic relationships among spanning tree weights hold. This work establishes new, non-equilibrium constraints governing the functional logic of driven matter.
main_problem: The research investigates how information-theoretic constraints, typically seen at equilibrium, persist or change when a physical system is driven far from thermodynamic equilibrium.
main_result: The authors identify 'energetic protection,' a mechanism where specific steady-state ratios remain exactly locked to their equilibrium values regardless of the driving strength, provided an underlying algebraic equality among spanning-tree weights holds.
method: The analysis uses graph theory applied to continuous-time Markov processes, focusing on calculating normalized response functions using arboreal distributions derived from spanning trees.
model_or_system: The model is a finite-state, continuous-time Markov process defined on a directed graph. The dynamics are perturbed by scaling specific transition rates (energetic edges) to drive the system away from equilibrium.
key_observables: The normalized ratio of steady-state probabilities ($K_{ij}$), which measures deviation from equilibrium, and the arboreal coefficients derived from spanning-tree weights.
important_parameters: The driving strength parameter ($m$), which scales the rates of the energetic edges; the algebraic equality between spanning-tree weights.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a unique steady state and relies heavily on deriving necessary algebraic constraints among spanning tree weights to prove robustness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how the response ratio behaves under driving, showing examples of monotonic change, perfect protection ($K_{ij}=1$), and the combination leading to a sharp 'thermodynamic switch.'
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing equilibrium constraints to analyzing single-edge driving (showing monotonicity), then introducing the condition for energetic protection via spanning-tree weight equalities, culminating in the construction of a programmable thermodynamic switch using two edges.
why_interesting: It provides novel, non-equilibrium invariants and robustness mechanisms that govern functional logic in driven systems, offering new constraints beyond standard detailed balance conditions relevant to open quantum systems dynamics.
